newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel little changed vs dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel little changed vs dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed almost unchanged against the dollar and the currency basket on Thursday in mixed trading, dealers said.

"Trading was mixed and quiet today with slightly more conversions of shekels into dollars. The shekel opened with a mild decline but...recovered following the weakening of the dollar in Europe," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.
"The dollar closed almost unchanged and the Bank of Israel remained out of the market," she added.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3580 shekels against 3.3570 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6631 shekels against 3.6625 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7372 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7425 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 2.0091 shekels after 2.0078 on Wednesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3570 shekels.
